mainTopic: A scholar's identification of women, who pays the סופר for each document, שטרי בירורין, and whether an אסמכתא is binding
overview: The גמרא first explains why רב ירמיה בר אבא could correct his testimony about a woman's identity: a צורבא מרבנן does not usually look closely at women. אביי adds that when a scholar does state firmly that he recognizes a woman, we trust him. אביי also advises that a scholar going to make קידושין should bring an עם הארץ along so nobody swaps the bride. The גמרא then works through the משנה about who pays the סופר. The husband pays for a גט because the פסוק says "he shall write" and "he shall give," though רבנן later put the cost on the woman so the husband would not delay. For each of the other documents, the גמרא shows the rule is needed even when the other side also gains. Next it explains שטרי בירורין in two ways, and shows that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's call for separate documents is not about מדת סדום. A new משנה argues whether an אסמכתא is binding, and the final הלכה is that it is not. The amud ends with the start of a משנה about a lender whose loan document was erased.

steps.title: A witness cannot change his testimony
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב ירמיה בר אבא's change of testimony with the rule that once a witness has testified, he cannot testify again differently.
steps.simpleTranslation: But once a witness has said his testimony, he cannot go back and say something new!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a problem with the earlier case of רב ירמיה בר אבא. He changed what he said about a woman's identity, but a witness is normally not allowed to do that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a known rule: כיון שהגיד שוב אינו חוזר ומגיד. Once testimony has been given, a later different version is not accepted. So how could רב ירמיה's second statement count?

keyTerms.meaning: he cannot go back and testify again (differently)

phrases.english: Once he has stated his testimony,
phrases.notes: This points back to רב ירמיה בר אבא's case from just before this, where he changed what he said about the woman.

phrases.english: he may not then go back and state something new!

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן שֶׁהִגִּיד, שׁוּב אֵינוֹ חוֹזֵר וּמַגִּיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the רב ירמיה בר אבא case from the previous section
steps.kashyaTarget: The acceptance of רב ירמיה בר אבא's revised testimony
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A witness's first testimony is final, so his retraction should not be accepted

steps.title: A Torah scholar does not look closely at women
steps.stepSummary: The answer: a צורבא מרבנן is not used to looking carefully at women, so his first identification was never a firm statement.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not the way of a Torah scholar to look carefully at women.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. A תלמיד חכם does not usually look closely at women, so his first identification was not careful. That is why he can correct it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule against changing testimony applies to a witness who spoke with real knowledge. Because a צורבא מרבנן avoids looking at women out of modesty, his first identification was not firm. This case is an exception to the usual rule; the rule itself still stands.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not say a תלמיד חכם is an unreliable witness in general. It only says he usually does not study women's faces closely.

phrases.english: It is not the way of a Torah scholar to look carefully.
phrases.notes: He means looking carefully at women to tell who is who, which a modest scholar avoids.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 1
steps.terutzResolutionType: Exception to the rule based on the witness's lack of careful knowledge
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every first testimony is final, so רב ירמיה could not take his back
steps.terutzMaskana: A scholar's quick identification of a woman was never firm testimony, so he may correct it

steps.title: The story of the receipt signed by רב ירמיה בר אבא
steps.stepSummary: A woman denied writing a receipt that רב ירמיה בר אבא had signed, and he told her firmly that it was her.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a receipt that רב ירמיה בר אבא had signed as a witness. A woman said to him: It wasn't me. He said to her: In fact, it was you.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story where רב ירמיה בר אבא firmly identifies a woman as the one in a receipt. This story sets up אביי's comment in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The woman wanted to collect her כתובה and claimed the receipt belonged to a different woman. רב ירמיה did not hesitate; he said clearly that she was the one. That raises a question: should we trust him, given what was just said about scholars?

keyTerms.meaning: a receipt (here, for payment of a כתובה)

phrases.english: There was a certain receipt
phrases.notes: A receipt showing a woman was already paid her כתובה, so she cannot collect it again.

phrases.aramaic: דַּהֲוָה חֲתִים עֲלֵיהּ רַב יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא.
phrases.english: on which Rav Yirmeya bar Abba was signed.
She said to him: It was not I.
He said to her: In fact, it was you.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא תְּבָרָא דַּהֲוָה חֲתִים עֲלֵיהּ רַב יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new story that tests the rule of step 2
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב ירמיה בר אבא firmly identified the woman as the one named in the receipt

steps.title: אביי: when a scholar is careful, he is trusted
steps.stepSummary: אביי rules that even though a צורבא מרבנן usually does not look closely, when he does state firmly that he recognizes someone, his word counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Even though it is not the way of a Torah scholar to look carefully, once he did look carefully, he looked carefully.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי draws the lesson from the story. A scholar who clearly says he is sure is trusted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 2 said a scholar's identification of a woman can be weak. אביי limits that: it only applies when he was not paying attention. Once he states firmly that he recognizes her, his testimony is fully accepted.

keyTerms.meaning: אביי, a leading אמורא of בבל
once he was careful, he was careful (we trust him)

steps.whatToRemember: A scholar usually does not look closely at women, so a casual identification can be corrected. But if he states firmly that he recognizes her, he is trusted.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Even though a Torah scholar
is not in the habit of looking carefully,
once he has looked carefully, he has looked carefully.
phrases.notes: In other words, when he says he is sure, we believe he really checked.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַף עַל גַּב דְּצוּרְבָּא מֵרַבָּנַן לָאו אוֹרְחֵיהּ לְמֵידַק, כֵּיוָן דְּדָק – דָּק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the halachic lesson from the story in step 3
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A scholar's firm, definite identification is trusted, even though his casual identifications are not

steps.title: A scholar betrothing a woman should bring an ordinary person along
steps.stepSummary: אביי advises a צורבא מרבנן going to make קידושין to take an עם הארץ with him, so that nobody can swap the woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: A Torah scholar who goes to betroth a woman should take an ordinary, unlearned person with him, in case they switch her for someone else.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives practical advice that follows from the same idea. Because a scholar does not look closely at women, he could be tricked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the scholar may not recognize the woman well, someone could hand him a different woman. An עם הארץ, who does look at people, can confirm she is the right one. The weakness found in steps 2–4 is turned into a practical precaution.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
A Torah scholar
who goes to betroth a woman
should take an ignoramus along with him,
lest they swap her on him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: הַאי צוּרְבָּא מֵרַבָּנַן דְּאָזֵיל לְקַדּוֹשֵׁי אִיתְּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Practical advice built on the idea that scholars do not look closely at women
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A scholar making קידושין should bring an עם הארץ to confirm the woman's identity

steps.title: Why does the husband pay the scribe?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה, which says the husband pays the סופר for the גט, and asks for the reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: "And the husband pays the fee." What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a line in the משנה and asks for its source. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says the husband pays the סופר's fee for writing a גט. The גמרא wants to know why the cost falls on him and not on the woman.

keyTerms.meaning: and the husband pays the fee

phrases.english: "And the husband gives the fee," etc.
What is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַבַּעַל נוֹתֵן שָׂכָר וְכוּ׳. מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the identification topic and returns to the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for the husband having to pay the סופר for the גט

steps.title: The verse says "he shall write" and "he shall give"
steps.stepSummary: The answer comes from the פסוק: the husband is the one commanded to write and give the גט, so he pays for it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the verse says: "He shall write" and "he shall give."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק showing that writing the גט is the husband's job.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה puts both writing and giving the גט on the husband. Since the writing is his responsibility, the cost of the writing is his too.

phrases.english: As the verse states:
"He shall write" and "he shall give."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק makes the husband responsible for writing the גט, so he pays the סופר

steps.title: Today the woman pays, so the husband won't delay
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that nowadays רבנן put the fee on the woman, so the husband will not hold up the גט by refusing to pay.
steps.simpleTranslation: And nowadays, when we don't do it this way, רבנן placed the cost on the woman, so that he will not delay the divorce.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why actual practice is different from the משנה. רבנן moved the cost to the woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By the תורה, the husband should pay. But a husband who did not want to pay could stall the divorce. So רבנן made the woman pay, which removes his excuse and helps her get the גט quickly.
steps.whatToRemember: By the תורה, the husband pays the סופר ("he shall write"). רבנן later put the cost on the woman so the husband would not delay the גט.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows רבנן changing who pays a cost in order to protect the woman's interest in being divorced quickly.

phrases.english: And nowadays, that we do not do so,
the Rabbis placed it upon the woman
phrases.notes: "It" means the duty to pay the סופר's fee.

phrases.english: so that he should not delay it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why current practice differs from the rule just derived
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Nowadays the woman pays the סופר, by rabbinic enactment, so the husband will not delay the גט

steps.title: Why say the borrower pays? It is obvious
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה that a סופר may write a loan document for the לוה alone, and the לוה pays. It asks: isn't that obvious?
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'We may write a loan document for the borrower even if the lender is not with him, etc.' (and the borrower pays). That is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה and complains that its ruling, that the לוה pays the סופר, is too obvious to need saying. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The לוה is the one who gets the money, so naturally he pays for the document. If the rule is that simple, the גמרא asks why the משנה bothered to state it.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious! (a challenge that a teaching is unnecessary)

steps.confusionAlert: The quote only says 'we write the document.' The part about who pays is hidden in the 'וכו׳'. The פשיטא is about who pays, not about writing the document.

phrases.english: We may write a document for the borrower

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין מַלְוֶה עִמּוֹ וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: even if the lender is not with him, etc.
phrases.notes: The 'etc.' covers the end of the משנה's line: the borrower pays the סופר. That is what the גמרא is asking about.

phrases.english: It is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the גט fee to the next line of the משנה about fees
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that the borrower pays
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The borrower is the one who benefits, so saying he pays adds nothing

steps.title: Needed for a joint-venture loan
steps.stepSummary: The rule is needed for an עיסקא, where the lender also earns from the deal. Even so, the לוה pays.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is needed for the case of an עיסקא (a joint business deal).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה's rule teaches something new in an עיסקא case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In an עיסקא the lender gets part of the profit, so he benefits too. You might think he should share the cost. The משנה teaches that the לוה still pays.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not needed (except for this case): the case where the teaching is still needed
A joint business deal where the lender shares in the profit

phrases.english: No, it is needed in a case of a joint venture.
phrases.notes: In an עיסקא the lender also profits, so you might have thought he should pay.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא of step 9
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the rule to a special case (לא צריכא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: When the lender profits too, he should pay
steps.terutzMaskana: Even in an עיסקא, the borrower pays

steps.title: Why say the buyer pays? It is obvious
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה that a bill of sale may be written for the seller alone, with the buyer paying, and asks: isn't that obvious?
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'We may write a document for the seller even if the buyer is not with him, etc.' (and the buyer pays). That is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the same פשיטא question on the next line of the משנה, about selling land. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The buyer gets the field and needs the document as proof, so of course he pays. The גמרא asks why this needed saying.

phrases.english: We may write a document for the seller

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין לוֹקֵחַ וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: even if the buyer is not with him, etc.
It is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same question applied to the next case in the משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that the buyer pays
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The buyer is the one who benefits, so of course he pays

steps.title: Needed when selling a bad field
steps.stepSummary: The rule is needed when the seller is glad to get rid of a poor field. Even then, the buyer pays.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is needed for someone who sells his field because it is bad.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה is talking about a case where the seller also gains from the sale.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the field is poor, the seller is happy to be rid of it, so he benefits too. You might think he should pay. The משנה teaches that the buyer still pays.

phrases.english: No, it is needed
in the case of one who sells his field because of its poor quality.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא of step 11
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the rule to a special case (לא צריכא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: When the seller is eager to sell, he should pay

steps.title: Why say the groom pays? It is obvious
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about documents of אירוסין, where the groom pays, and asks: isn't that obvious?
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'We may not write documents of betrothal, etc.' (without both sides, and the groom pays). That is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the same פשיטא question on the משנה's line about marriage documents. The answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The groom is the one acquiring a wife, so naturally he pays the סופר. The גמרא asks why the משנה needed to say it.

phrases.english: We may not write documents of betrothal, etc.
It is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same question applied to the third case in the משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that the groom pays
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The groom is the one who gains, so of course he pays

steps.title: Needed even when the groom is a Torah scholar
steps.stepSummary: The rule is needed even for a צורבא מרבנן groom, whom the father-in-law is happy to bring into the family. Even then, the groom pays.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is needed even for a Torah scholar, where the father-in-law is pleased to bring him into his family.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the rule teaches something new when the bride's family is the one eager for the match.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the groom is a צורבא מרבנן, the bride's father gains a lot from the match. You might think he should pay the סופר. The משנה teaches that the groom still pays.

keyTerms.meaning: To bring him close (into the family)

phrases.english: No, it is needed
to teach that even with a Torah scholar,
where his father-in-law is pleased to bring him into the family, (the groom still pays).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא of step 13
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the rule to a special case (לא צריכא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: When the father-in-law is eager for the match, he should pay
steps.terutzMaskana: Even with a צורבא מרבנן, the groom pays

steps.title: Why say the sharecropper pays? It is obvious
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about contracts for an אריס or קבלן, who pays the סופר, and asks: isn't that obvious?
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'We may not write contracts for sharecropping and contracting, etc.' (without both sides, and the worker pays). That is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the same פשיטא question on the last of the משנה's cases about who pays the סופר. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The contract protects the אריס's right to work the field, so he is the one who needs it and pays for it. The גמרא asks why this had to be said.

keyTerms.meaning: Sharecropping: working someone's field for a share of the crop
Contracting: taking on a field for a set payment

phrases.aramaic: אֵין כּוֹתְבִין שְׁטַר אֲרִיסוּת וְקַבְּלָנוּת וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: We may not write contracts for sharecropping and contracting, etc.
It is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same question applied to the fourth case in the משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that the sharecropper or contractor pays
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The contract serves the worker, so of course he pays

steps.title: Needed even for a fallow field
steps.stepSummary: The rule is needed for a fallow field, where the deal favors the owner. Even then, the אריס pays.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is needed in the case of a fallow field.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה teaches something new when the field is fallow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Taking on a fallow field is a poor deal for the worker, and the owner is the one who gains. You might think the owner should pay. The משנה teaches that the worker still pays.

keyTerms.meaning: A fallow field that has not been worked

steps.whatToRemember: In all four cases the pattern is the same. The side the document is written for, the one who mainly needs it, pays the סופר. This holds even when the other side also gains from the deal.

phrases.english: No, it is needed in the case of a fallow field.
phrases.notes: A fallow field takes a lot of work, so here the deal is better for the owner than for the worker.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא of step 15 and closes the series
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the rule to a special case (לא צריכא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: When the deal favors the owner, he should pay
steps.terutzMaskana: Even with a fallow field, the sharecropper or contractor pays

steps.title: What are documents of selection?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה that שטרי בירורין are written only with both sides' consent, and asks what these documents are.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: We do not write documents of בירורין except with the consent of both sides, etc. What are these "documents of בירורין"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new line of the משנה and asks what the term שטרי בירורין means. This sets up the two answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה uses a term without defining it. Before we can understand why both sides must agree, we need to know what kind of document this is.

keyTerms.meaning: Documents of selection or clarification. What exactly they are is the question here.
With the consent of both of them

phrases.english: We do not write documents of selection
except with the consent of both of them, etc.
phrases.notes: "Both of them" means the two sides in the court case.

phrases.english: What are "documents of selection"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new clause of the משנה after the discussion about who pays the סופר.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The definition of the term שטרי בירורין.

steps.title: First answer: documents of claims
steps.stepSummary: In בבל they explained that שטרי בירורין are documents that record each side's claims.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here in בבל they explained: these are documents of claims.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the first answer. The documents write down what each side is claiming in the case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On this reading, the document is a record of the arguments. So it makes sense that both sides must agree before it is written down.

phrases.english: Here they explained:
documents of claims.
phrases.notes: These are papers that write down what each side argued in court.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: שטרי בירורין are written records of the litigants' claims.

steps.title: Second answer: each side picks a judge
steps.stepSummary: רב ירמיה בר אבא says שטרי בירורין record how the judges were chosen, with each side choosing one judge.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ירמיה בר אבא said: This one chooses one judge for himself, and that one chooses one judge for himself.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ירמיה בר אבא gives a different explanation. The documents record the choosing of the judges.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word בירורין comes from "choosing." Here it refers to the process where each side picks a judge. The document is a record of who was picked, not of the claims.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who gives the second explanation

phrases.english: רב ירמיה בר אבא said:
This one chooses one for himself,
and that one chooses one for himself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to the question of step 17, disagreeing with step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: שטרי בירורין record the choosing of the judges, where each side picks one.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two ways to explain שטרי בירורין: records of the claims (טענתא), or records of the judges each side chose.

steps.title: Is the argument about forcing someone to stop acting selfishly?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, who says each side gets his own document. It suggests he and the תנא קמא argue about whether we force someone to stop acting with מדת סדום.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: For the two of them we write two documents, one for this one by himself and one for that one by himself. Shall we say they argue about whether we force someone against מדת סדום? One master holds we force him, and the other holds we do not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's view and suggests what the argument with the תנא קמא is based on. This proposal will be tested in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that one side refuses to share a single document and demands separate ones, which costs the other side more. If we force a person not to act with מדת סדום, the תנא קמא would make him share one document. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל would hold we do not force him, so each side gets his own.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? It introduces a suggestion the גמרא may reject.
The trait of סדום: being selfish for no good reason
By himself, his own separate one

steps.confusionAlert: לֵימָא usually opens a suggestion that the גמרא is about to reject. Don't treat it as the final answer.

phrases.english: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says:
for the two of them we write two documents,
one for this one by himself and one for that one by himself.
Shall we say that about forcing someone against the trait of סדום
phrases.notes: מדת סדום means refusing to help someone even when it would not cost you anything.

phrases.english: they argue,
so that one master holds: we force him,
phrases.notes: "One master" is the תנא קמא of the משנה.

phrases.english: and the other master holds: we do not force him?

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא בְּכוֹפִין עַל מִדַּת סְדוֹם קָא מִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns to the next clause of the משנה and proposes a basis for the argument in it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the argument between the תנא קמא and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל depends on כופין על מדת סדום.

steps.title: Everyone agrees we force; there is a real reason for separate documents
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion. Everyone agrees we force a person not to act with מדת סדום. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל allows separate documents because the litigant has a real concern: he does not want his claims sitting together with his opponent's.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Everyone agrees that we force him. Here, this is the reason of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: the litigant says to the other one, "I am not comfortable having your claims together with my claims, because to me you are like a lion lying in ambush."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says the argument has nothing to do with מדת סדום. It explains that asking for a separate document is not selfish, because the person has a real reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מדת סדום only applies when a refusal has no real reason behind it. Here the litigant fears his opponent, who is like a lion in ambush, could use a shared document against him. So even the opinion that forces against מדת סדום agrees he can ask for his own document.

keyTerms.meaning: I am not comfortable with it

steps.whatToRemember: The argument is not about מדת סדום, since all agree we force against it. A litigant may ask for his own separate document because he fears his opponent, who is "like a lion in ambush."
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that refusing to cooperate is not מדת סדום when the person has a real reason to protect himself.

phrases.english: No, everyone agrees that we force him;

phrases.aramaic: וְהָכָא הַיְינוּ טַעְמָא דְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל –
phrases.english: and here, this is the reason of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל:
because he says to him:
phrases.notes: "He" is the litigant who wants his own document. "Him" is the other side.

phrases.english: I am not comfortable
having your claims together with my claims,
because you seem to me
like a lion lying in ambush.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion of step 20 and gives a different reason for רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that the argument depends on כופין על מדת סדום.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The suggestion assumed that asking for separate documents is pointless selfishness. In fact the litigant has a real concern about his opponent.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: All agree כופין על מדת סדום. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל allows separate documents because a litigant has a real reason not to have his claims written alongside his opponent's.

steps.title: A deadline promise about a partly paid debt
steps.stepSummary: A borrower paid part of his debt and left the שטר with a trustee. He said that if he did not pay the rest by a certain day, the trustee should give the lender the full שטר. The deadline passed. רבי יוסי says the trustee gives it, and רבי יהודה says he does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Someone paid part of his debt and gave his loan document to a third person to hold. He told him: 'If I don't give you the rest between now and such-and-such a day, give the lender his document.' The day came and he did not pay. רבי יוסי says: the holder should give it. רבי יהודה says: he should not give it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It describes a borrower who made a deadline promise with a penalty, and two תנאים who argue about whether that promise is enforced.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The שטר held by the trustee still records the full loan amount. If the trustee hands it over, the lender can collect the full amount written in it, even though part was already paid. That is a penalty for missing the deadline. רבי יוסי holds the borrower to his word, and רבי יהודה does not.

keyTerms.meaning: He gave something to a third party (a שָׁלִישׁ) to hold
Such-and-such a day, a set date

phrases.english: MISHNA: One who repaid part of his debt
and deposited his promissory note with a third party,
and he said to him [the third party]:
If I have not given you [the rest of the money]
from now until such-and-such a day,
give him [the lender] his note,
and the time arrived and he did not give,
Rabbi Yosei says: he should give [the note to the lender];
Rabbi Yehuda says: he should not give it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה after the discussion of שטרי בירורין ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the deadline passes, רבי יוסי says the trustee gives the full שטר to the lender. רבי יהודה says he does not.

steps.title: What is the root of their argument?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which underlying principle רבי יוסי and רבי יהודה disagree about.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: About what do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the argument in the משנה. This line sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only gives the two rulings. The גמרא wants to find the general legal principle that explains why one says 'give' and the other says 'don't give.'

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה

phrases.english: GEMARA: With regard to what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the principle behind the dispute in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The underlying principle that divides רבי יוסי and רבי יהודה.

steps.title: They argue about whether an אסמכתא is binding
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי holds that an אסמכתא is binding, and רבי יהודה holds that it is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי holds an אסמכתא takes effect. רבי יהודה holds an אסמכתא does not take effect.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question. The argument is about אסמכתא, a promise a person makes because he is sure he will never have to keep it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The borrower agreed to the penalty because he expected to pay on time. רבי יוסי says he is still bound by what he agreed to. רבי יהודה says that kind of promise was never truly meant, so it does not take effect.

keyTerms.meaning: A promise made while relying on the belief that it will never come due
It takes effect / it is binding

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבי יהודה is calling the borrower a liar. He agrees the borrower said the words. He only holds that this kind of promise does not create a binding obligation.
steps.whyThisMatters: אסמכתא is a major rule in monetary law. It affects penalty clauses and conditional promises throughout ש״ס.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei holds: an asmakhta effects acquisition,
phrases.notes: An אסמכתא is a promise you make because you feel sure you'll never have to keep it, like this deadline promise.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה סָבַר: אַסְמַכְתָּא לָא קָנְיָא.
phrases.english: and Rabbi Yehuda holds: an asmakhta does not effect acquisition.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 23.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The dispute is whether an אסמכתא is binding: רבי יוסי says yes, רבי יהודה says no.

steps.title: רב rules like רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: Through a chain of teachers, רב rules that the הלכה follows רבי יוסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה in the name of רב: the הלכה follows רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ruling on the dispute. רב says the הלכה is like רבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This means the trustee should give the שטר to the lender, so the אסמכתא would be binding.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical law follows the opinion of
An אמורא who reports the ruling
רב נחמן's teacher, who heard it from רב

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rav Naḥman says that Rabba bar Avuh says that Rav says:
The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Yosei.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a ruling on the dispute explained in step 24.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבי יוסי: an אסמכתא is binding here.

steps.title: רבי אמי feels bound by רבי יוחנן's ruling
steps.stepSummary: When people asked רבי אמי about this case, he said that רבי יוחנן had taught again and again that the הלכה follows רבי יוסי, so he could not rule otherwise.
steps.simpleTranslation: When they came before רבי אמי, he told them: since רבי יוחנן taught us once and twice that the הלכה follows רבי יוסי, what can I do?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second report. In the name of רבי יוחנן, it also says the הלכה is like רבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now both רב and רבי יוחנן rule like רבי יוסי. רבי אמי's words 'what can I do?' show that he felt he had to follow his teacher's repeated ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: A first and second time, meaning repeatedly

phrases.english: When they came before Rabbi Ami,
he said to them: But since
Rabbi Yoḥanan teaches us
a first time and a second time
that the halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Yosei,
what can I do?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second report, from רבי יוחנן, that matches רב's ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן repeatedly ruled like רבי יוסי, and רבי אמי felt bound to follow that.

steps.title: The final ruling: not like רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the הלכה does not follow רבי יוסי. An אסמכתא is not binding.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the הלכה is not like רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its final word. Even though רב and רבי יוחנן were quoted, the actual הלכה is NOT like רבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This sides with רבי יהודה. An אסמכתא does not take effect, so the trustee does not give the full שטר to the lender.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוסי says an אסמכתא is binding, and רבי יהודה says it is not. Although רב and רבי יוחנן ruled like רבי יוסי, the final הלכה is that an אסמכתא is not binding, so the trustee keeps the שטר.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't stop reading after the rulings of רב and רבי יוחנן! The last line reverses them, and that last line is the final הלכה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical rule that a penalty promise based on אסמכתא cannot be enforced.

phrases.english: But the halakha is not in accordance with Rabbi Yosei.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Overrides the rulings of steps 25 and 26 with the final הלכה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows רבי יהודה: an אסמכתא is not binding, and the trustee does not hand over the שטר.

steps.title: A lender whose loan document was erased gets it validated by the court
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that if a lender's שטר חוב was erased, he brings witnesses to בית דין, and the court writes a קיום stating that so-and-so's document was erased on a certain day.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If someone's loan document was erased, he brings witnesses about it, comes before the court, and they write a validation for him: 'So-and-so, son of so-and-so, had his document erased on such-and-such a day,'
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins, teaching how a lender can save a loan document that got erased. It starts quoting the court's written statement, and that quote continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An erased שטר חוב cannot be used to collect, because no one can read what it says. The משנה's fix: witnesses who know about the document testify, and בית דין writes its own official statement (a קיום) recording that this person's document was erased. That court document then stands in place of the ruined one.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for מַתְנִיתִין, 'our משנה'. This marks the start of a new משנה.
A loan document, a written record of a debt.
A validation: an official court statement confirming a document.
So-and-so; a placeholder for a real name or date.

steps.confusionAlert: The court is not judging a fight between the lender and the borrower here. It is just writing an official record so that the lender's erased document does not become useless.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One whose promissory note was erased
sets up witnesses about it,
phrases.notes: These are witnesses who can speak about the erased document.

phrases.english: and comes before the court,
and they make a validation for him:
'So-and-so, son of so-and-so,'
his document was erased on such-and-such a day,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה begins after the conclusion about אסמכתא in step 27. It does not depend on that discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A lender whose שטר חוב was erased may bring witnesses to בית דין, and the court writes a קיום recording the erased document.
